name: Vantage Data Centers
founded: June 2010 (Santa Clara, CA, backed by Silver Lake; acquired by a Digital Colony/DigitalBridge-led consortium in 2017)
ownership: private (DigitalBridge-managed platform; co-investors include Silver Lake, PSP Investments, GIC, ADIA, AustralianSuper, MEAG, WAFRA, GCM Grosvenor and Pantheon)
summary: BOTTOM LINE UP FRONT: Vantage Data Centers is the giga-scale wholesale landlord at the center of Stargate's third-party buildout — 41 campuses across five continents and roughly 9GW of power capacity (per the February 2026 Altarea joint release), anchored by two Oracle/OpenAI mega-campuses: Frontier in Shackelford County, Texas (1.4GW, $25B+, off-grid on a 700MW VoltaGrid gas microgrid) and Lighthouse in Port Washington, Wisconsin (902MW, $15B+), together financed by a record $38B bank debt package led by JPMorgan and MUFG (per Bloomberg, Oct 2025). The company invented the data-center securitization (industry-first $1.125B ABS, 2018) and has since run 10+ securitizations including the first sterling and first euro data-center ABS. On 13 August 2026 Reuters reported Vantage is exploring an IPO at a valuation of about $100B — raising around $10B as soon as 2027 — or a sale; deliberations are early-stage and unconfirmed by the company. BACKGROUND: Denver-headquartered; founded June 2010 in Santa Clara with Silver Lake backing; Sureel Choksi (ex-Level 3 CFO, ex-Silver Lake operating executive) has been CEO since 2013. A Digital Colony (now DigitalBridge)-led consortium acquired the company from Silver Lake in 2017; Silver Lake returned as co-lead of the $9.2B equity investment completed June 2024 (announced at $6.4B in January 2024, upsized at close). The platform is organized as three regionally financed businesses — North America (16 campuses), EMEA (15 campuses, entering France as a tenth market), APAC (9 campuses, 1GW operational and planned) — each carrying its own investor group: AustralianSuper (€1.5B, 2023), GIC and MEAG (€1.4B, Dec 2024) in EMEA; GIC and ADIA ($1.6B, closed Nov 2025) in APAC. Vantage secured a record $13B of incremental debt and equity in 2024 and states it has raised more than $60B globally since late 2024. Employees 1,700+ at year-end 2024; no revenue or EBITDA figures are disclosed.
ecosystemRole: We assess Vantage as the most consequential private wholesale developer-landlord in this ecosystem — the company that turned build-to-suit hyperscale campuses into a repeatable, securitizable product and is now executing the largest third-party piece of the Oracle/OpenAI Stargate program. Basis: company releases and trade coverage — two named Stargate campuses (1.4GW Texas, 902MW Wisconsin), a 700MW behind-the-meter microgrid with VoltaGrid plus an up-to-1GW generation partnership with Liberty Energy, an OCP Foundation Advisory Board seat (operator perspective), and a financing franchise that originated the data-center ABS asset class in 2018. For power-chain and construction vendors, Vantage is a standardized global procurement machine: one 'sustainable by design' blueprint (closed-loop chilled water, near-zero WUE, liquid-to-liquid cooling to 250kW+ racks) replicated across 41 campuses, with a newly created global product organization and chief procurement office (ex-Equinix) centralizing sourcing across power, cooling, construction and network.

productsAndServices.name: North America hyperscale campuses (core business)
productsAndServices.description: Build-own-operate wholesale campuses leased long-term to hyperscalers across 16 North American locations — now led by two AI giga-campuses for the Oracle/OpenAI Stargate program: Frontier, Shackelford County, TX (1.4GW critical IT, 10 buildings, 3.7M sq ft, $25B+, first building H2 2026, campus complete 2028) and Lighthouse, Port Washington, WI (902MW, 4 buildings, 2.5M sq ft, $15B+, complete 2028). The established fleet spans Virginia (4 campuses, 782MW statewide, ~$8B invested), Nevada (NV1: 224MW, ~$3B, first two buildings fully leased), New Albany, OH (192MW, 3 pre-leased buildings, first operational Dec 2025), Fredericksburg, VA (VA4: 192MW, $2B, first building late 2027), Phoenix (160MW), Quincy, WA (89MW), Santa Clara (75MW — 'largest in Silicon Valley') and Canada (4 campuses, 178MW, ~CAD$2.5B).
highlights: Two named Stargate campuses totaling ~2.3GW under construction, financed by a record $38B loan package (Bloomberg, Oct 2025)
Frontier runs off-grid on a 700MW VoltaGrid natural-gas microgrid — 210 Jenbacher engines (197 prime + 13 backup) supporting up to 1.4GW of compute
Fredericksburg VA4 is the fleet's first campus with CDU-based liquid-to-liquid cooling for 100% of IT load
productsAndServices.positioning: One of the few developers repeatedly delivering 500MW-and-larger campuses on multiple continents (Data Center Frontier's assessment) — larger private-platform scale than Aligned or STACK, wholesale/build-to-suit focus unlike interconnection-led Equinix, and unlike REITs it recycles capital through securitization rather than public equity.
productsAndServices.soldThrough: Long-term wholesale leases and build-to-suit agreements direct with hyperscalers and AI platforms; campus-level debt (green loans, ABS, private-IG construction loans) raised against the leases.
targetSegments: Hyperscalers (Oracle for OpenAI/Stargate; unnamed cloud majors)
productsAndServices.roadmap: Frontier first building H2 2026, complete 2028; Lighthouse complete 2028; NV1 first building Q2 2026; VA4 first building late 2027; QC24 (Quebec City, 32MW) early 2027.

productsAndServices.name: EMEA platform (15 campuses, 10 markets)
productsAndServices.description: Wholesale campuses across Germany (Berlin I-II, Frankfurt I-II), UK (Cardiff/Newport CWL1 — 148MW, one of Europe's largest, operational since 2010; London LHR1-2), Switzerland (Zurich I-II), Italy (Milan MXP1-2), Poland (Warsaw), Ireland (Dublin, 52MW), South Africa (Johannesburg I-II) and, from February 2026, France — a partnership with Altarea to develop one of France's largest AI/cloud campuses near Bordeaux on a site with a 400MW grid connection already secured. South Wales is the flagship AI cluster: Vantage expects to deliver more than 1GW of AI-ready capacity across Newport, Bridgend and Bro Tathan, and in August 2026 signed Nebius as the first commercial capacity commitment in the UK's South Wales AI Growth Zone.
highlights: Italy recognized Vantage's ~€4B, 8-year program as nationally strategic infrastructure (Council of Ministers, Oct 2025)
MXP2 Milan: €350M, 32MW, first phase spring 2026; LHR2 London: 20MW, £250M, BREEAM Excellent with district-heating waste-heat reuse
€2.2B of new EMEA debt raised in the 12 months to June 2025
productsAndServices.positioning: Differentiated by ABS-financed scale in markets where peers rely on bank debt — Vantage completed the first sterling (2024) and first euro (2025) data-center securitizations in EMEA; CWL1's private 400kV SuperGrid substation is a structural power advantage in the UK.
productsAndServices.soldThrough: Long-term wholesale leases to hyperscale, cloud, AI and public-sector customers; joint development with local partners (Altarea in France).
productsAndServices.roadmap: Bordeaux campus development with Altarea (timeline TBD); >1GW South Wales buildout; MXP2 phase 1 spring 2026.

productsAndServices.name: APAC platform (1GW operational and planned)
productsAndServices.description: Nine campuses across Malaysia, Hong Kong, Taiwan, Japan and Australia, built from the 2021 Agile Data Centers and PCCW data-center acquisitions and scaled by a $1.6B GIC/ADIA equity investment (closed Nov 2025) that also funded the acquisition of Yondr's JHB1 campus in Sedenak Tech Park, Johor, Malaysia — 300MW+ across three buildings on ~73 acres inside the Johor-Singapore Special Economic Zone, with direct-to-chip liquid cooling. Malaysia is the growth engine: KUL1 Cyberjaya completed (four buildings; the 16MW KUL14 fully leased to a single customer, Dec 2025) and a second Cyberjaya campus under development cited at over 400MW of total capacity.
highlights: JHB1 is one of Southeast Asia's largest hyperscale campuses — Vantage's third Malaysian campus
Osaka (68MW) and Taipei (16MW first facility, opened July 2024) anchor North Asia; three Hong Kong facilities from the PCCW deal
First greenfield hyperscale data-center financing in Taiwan (US$64M) and inaugural APAC bonds (US$114M, CGIF-guaranteed)
productsAndServices.positioning: Positioned as one of the largest providers of sustainable AI/cloud infrastructure in APAC (company claim); competes with AirTrunk, Equinix and ST Telemedia in the Johor/Singapore corridor where JHB1's scale and SEZ location are the wedge.
productsAndServices.soldThrough: Wholesale leases; country leadership under a dedicated Malaysia managing director (ex-Oracle Malaysia MD Fitri Abdullah, appointed Feb 2026).
targetSegments: Cloud and AI providers in Japan, Taiwan, Hong Kong, Australia
productsAndServices.roadmap: JHB1 full 300MW+ buildout across three buildings; Cyberjaya II expansion toward 400MW+.

productsAndServices.name: Energy & powered-land platform (behind-the-meter generation)
productsAndServices.description: A productized answer to grid constraints: partnerships that bolt dispatchable generation onto Vantage campuses. VoltaGrid (Feb 2025) is deploying more than 1GW of prime natural-gas microgrid capacity across the North America portfolio — including Frontier's 700MW off-grid plant (210 Jenbacher reciprocating engines, TCEQ-approved) — with up to 98% criteria-pollutant emissions reduction and hydrogen/RNG optionality. Liberty Energy (Jan 2026) adds up to 1GW of power agreements within five years through Liberty Power Innovations, including a 400MW reservation of 2027 generation capacity, owned and operated by LPI as long-term power services. At Lighthouse, Vantage is enabling new zero-emission generation (solar, wind, battery) with 70% allocated to the campus and 30% to Wisconsin consumers, underwriting 100% of the power infrastructure via a dedicated WEC Energy rate plus $175M+ of regional infrastructure upgrades.
highlights: Frontier operates fully off-grid — sidestepping interconnection queues that run up to five years
Ratepayer Protection Pledge signed July 2026: data centers should pay for the energy infrastructure their demand creates
Company frames the model as protecting communities from cost/supply strain while adding grid resilience
productsAndServices.positioning: Against Crusoe's owned energy stack and Aligned's grid-first siting, Vantage buys speed through partnership structures — generation is owned/operated by VoltaGrid or Liberty, keeping Vantage's balance sheet on buildings while still controlling delivery timelines.
productsAndServices.soldThrough: Long-term power services agreements between the energy partner (LPI/VoltaGrid) and Vantage or its data-center end-users.
targetSegments: Vantage's own campuses in grid-constrained North American markets
productsAndServices.roadmap: 400MW of LPI 2027 generation reserved; VoltaGrid deployments scale with campus starts; expansion potential beyond 1GW under both partnerships.

productsAndServices.name: Capital-markets franchise (securitization & green finance)
productsAndServices.description: A genuinely productized funding capability that the rest of the industry copied: Vantage completed the industry's first data-center securitization in February 2018 ($1.125B, rated A- by S&P), its 10th securitization by mid-2024, the first-ever EMEA data-center ABS in sterling (£600M, June 2024), the first euro data-center ABS (€640M, June 2025) and a £254M tap plus new £54M Class B tranche in January 2026 (Class A-2 rated A-/A(low)/A by S&P, Morningstar DBRS and Scope; Class B BBB-/BBB). The green-loan stack includes a $5.75B North America corporate facility (upsized $2.75B in June 2025, Wells Fargo-led) and a $2.25B New Albany construction loan that was among the industry's first construction financings with private investment-grade ratings from two agencies (MUFG/SocGen-led). Capped by the ~$38B JPMorgan/MUFG-led package for the two Stargate campuses ($23.25B Texas, $14.75B Wisconsin, ~4-year, ~SOFR+250 per Bloomberg) — the largest AI-infrastructure financing to date.
highlights: More than $60B raised globally since late 2024 (company statement); record $13B of incremental funding in 2024
All EMEA ABS carry Green Bond designations under Vantage's Green Finance Framework (Sustainalytics SPO)
Regional equity syndication is part of the product: DigitalBridge/Silver Lake ($9.2B, 2024), AustralianSuper/GIC/MEAG (EMEA), GIC/ADIA (APAC $1.6B, 2025)
productsAndServices.positioning: The deepest, longest-running securitization program in the sector — a funding-cost and repeatability advantage over developers dependent on private credit (e.g. the 12.75% preferred layers seen at miner-pivot landlords).
productsAndServices.soldThrough: 144A/Reg-S securitized notes, syndicated green loans, and platform-level equity placements arranged by a dedicated global capital-markets team.
productsAndServices.roadmap: Reuters (Aug 13, 2026): exploring an IPO at ~$100B valuation raising ~$10B as soon as 2027, or a sale — early-stage, no formal process launched.

strategyRead: (High confidence) We assess Vantage is being positioned for a 2027 liquidity event — IPO or sale. Basis: a public-company CFO (Beasley) hired March 2026 after six other C-suite seats turned over in twelve months, a standalone global product organization stood up December 2025, DigitalBridge consolidating sponsor-family assets into the platform (Yondr JHB1, Nov 2025), tightening disclosure discipline (the customary January growth recap skipped for the first time since at least 2021), and Reuters' August 2026 report of a ~$100B IPO exploration.

(High confidence) We assess Stargate concentration is now Vantage's defining exposure — growth engine and largest single risk at once. Basis: the two Oracle/OpenAI campuses (Frontier 1.4GW / Lighthouse 902MW, $40B+ of combined build) dwarf every prior program and sit behind a record ~$38B, roughly four-year bank package priced around +250bps — refinancing outcomes are tied to the OpenAI complex's credit trajectory in a way no earlier Vantage financing was tied to any single tenant.

(High confidence) We assess behind-the-meter gas generation has become a deliberate time-to-power product rather than a bridge. Basis: Frontier runs fully off-grid on a 700MW VoltaGrid microgrid (210 Jenbacher engines per TCEQ filings), backed by two separate gigawatt-class generation partnerships (VoltaGrid, Feb 2025; Liberty Energy, Jan 2026, with 400MW of 2027 capacity reserved) — while the Ratepayer Protection Pledge supplies the political cover for burning gas next to constrained grids.

(Moderate confidence) We assess the capital-markets franchise, more than design IP, is the durable moat. Basis: Vantage originated the data-center ABS asset class (2018), opened the sterling and euro DC-ABS markets, runs regionally ring-fenced equity (AustralianSuper/GIC/MEAG in EMEA, GIC/ADIA in APAC), and claims $60B+ raised globally since late 2024 — an out-financing capability peers have imitated but not matched.

(Moderate confidence) We assess community-consent risk is rising faster than the siting playbook is adapting. Basis: Port Washington passed the nation's first anti-data-center referendum (Apr 2026, 66%) around the Lighthouse TIF; newer market entries favor pre-secured power and local partners (Altarea's 400MW Bordeaux connection, pre-leased Reno buildings) — a pattern consistent with engineering around local friction rather than resolving it.

metrics.name: Securitizations
metrics.actual: Industry's first data-center ABS: $1.125B, February 2018 (A- by S&P); 10th securitization completed by June 2024. North America: +$530M (Nov 2021), +$1.35B (Oct 2023). EMEA: £600M first sterling DC ABS (June 2024), €640M first euro DC ABS + €80M VFN (June 2025), £200M tap + £54M Class B (January 2026; A-/A(low)/A senior, BBB-/BBB Class B by S&P, Morningstar DBRS, Scope)
metrics.result: The longest-running securitization franchise in the sector; EMEA notes carry Green Bond designations (Sustainalytics SPO)

metrics.name: Green loans (North America)
metrics.actual: $3B borrowing-base facility (April 2024, Wells Fargo-led) upsized $2.75B to $5.75B (June 2025); $2.25B New Albany construction loan with private investment-grade ratings from two agencies (June 2025, MUFG/Societe Generale-led); $300M VA13 green loan (2022)
metrics.result: Company cited $8B total available for North America expansion as of mid-2025

metrics.name: Stargate campus financing
metrics.actual: ~$38B bank package led by JPMorgan and MUFG — $23.25B Frontier (TX), $14.75B Lighthouse (WI); ~4-year tenor, ~250bps over benchmark; Wells Fargo and Goldman Sachs participating (Bloomberg, Oct 23, 2025)
metrics.result: The largest AI-infrastructure debt financing to date at pricing

metrics.name: APAC debt
metrics.actual: US$114M-equivalent CGIF-guaranteed bonds (Dec 2024, inaugural APAC issuance); US$64M loan from CTBC and Cathay United — Taiwan's first greenfield hyperscale DC financing (March 2024)
metrics.result: Small but first-of-kind instruments opening local funding markets

periods.commentary: Run-rate: a record $13B of incremental debt and equity secured in 2024 (company release, Jan 2025); more than $60B raised globally since late 2024 per the company's own capital-markets attribution. €2.2B of EMEA debt raised in the 12 months to June 2025.

metrics.name: Platform
metrics.actual: 41 campus locations across five continents (company site, 2026); 'more than 40 hyperscale campuses and 9GW of power capacity' per the Altarea joint release (Feb 2026); >2.6GW of planned and existing global IT capacity cited at the January 2025 annual recap
metrics.result: The 9GW figure is power capacity including development pipeline; built IT capacity is materially lower

metrics.name: Regional footprints
metrics.actual: Virginia 782MW / ~$8B across four campuses; Canada 178MW / ~CAD$2.5B; APAC 1GW operational and planned; South Wales >1GW planned

periods.commentary: Collection gap: Vantage discloses no revenue, EBITDA, leverage or consolidated balance-sheet figures — it is private with no public filings, and no analyst consensus exists, so every 'expected' field is left empty. A second gap: the company published annual growth recaps each January through 2025 but issued none in January 2026, leaving FY2025 platform-wide funding and capacity totals unstated; the trailing figures above are assembled from individual releases.
